name: 2I/Borisov
credit: Hui, Ye, Föhring, Hung and Tholen (2020), AJ 160, 92, nucleus size from non-gravitational acceleration
shapeMeaning: No image resolves the nucleus. Hubble limits its radius to at most 0.5 km at assumed geometric albedo 0.04, and its non-gravitational acceleration requires at least 0.2 km at assumed density 500 kg/m³ (Jewitt et al. 2020). Hui et al. (2020) estimate it is most likely at most 0.4 km. The display is a 0.4 km sphere: an estimate inside those bounds, not a measured size or shape.
orientationMeaning: Pole RA 205°, Dec 52° (obliquity 30°), fitted to coma anisotropy by Kim et al. (2020); the prime meridian and spin phase are arbitrary and the period is not determined.
introduction: It swung past the Sun in December 2019, trailing gas like an ordinary comet. Its nucleus was never resolved; the sphere shown is an estimated size.
card: The second interstellar object seen passing through the Solar System, and the first clearly active comet.
datasetSummary: A sphere of estimated size inside Hubble limits, turned on the pole fitted to its coma; the true shape is unknown.
survey: Included: Hui et al. (2020) nucleus radius most likely at most 0.4 km from non-gravitational acceleration and CO production.
Included as bounds: Jewitt et al. (2020) Hubble coma modelling, radius at most 0.5 km (pV 0.04), and at least 0.2 km from acceleration (density 500 kg/m³).
Included: Kim et al. (2020) pole RA 205°, Dec 52° from coma anisotropy.
Excluded: coma photographs and artist impressions as surface textures; the nucleus is unresolved. The 2020 outburst fragments are not modelled.
Included: JPL Horizons 2026-09-03 heliocentric osculating trajectory and independent vectors.
